headline: Acquisition boosts revenue, but profit swings to a loss

kpis.label: Income from continuing operations before interest and taxes
Income from continuing operations before interest and taxes

summary_short: Revenue rose 32.3% y/y to $548.3M on the acquired VI Business, but Teleflex swung to a $8.2M net loss (-$0.18 diluted EPS) from $95.0M net income a year ago as tariffs and $16.8M of divestiture restructuring charges outweighed the gains — a sharp sequential improvement from Q4 2025's $714.3M writedown-driven loss.
summary_long: Revenue grew $134.0M (32.3%) mostly on $99.1M from the acquired VI Business plus higher volumes and favorable FX. Gross margin fell 560bps to 56.1% on 2025 tariffs, VI step-up amortization, and higher quality/logistics costs. SG&A and R&D rose on VI integration. The company booked $16.8M of restructuring/separation costs tied to the pending Strategic Divestitures (Acute Care, IU, OEM) and the VI plan, plus a $29.0M valuation-allowance adjustment on assets held for sale. Net loss was $8.2M (-$0.18 diluted EPS), a sharp sequential improvement from Q4 2025's $714.3M loss. Adjusted diluted EPS was $1.39 vs $1.44 a year ago. Operating cash flow rose to $46.7M. The company maintained full-year 2026 guidance: revenue growth 14.4%-15.4%, adjusted EPS $6.25-$6.55.

drivers.explanation: The acquired VI Business drove revenue growth, but tariffs, VI integration/step-up amortization costs, and Strategic Divestitures restructuring/separation charges pushed the company to a net loss, even as results improved sharply from Q4 2025's impairment-driven loss.
Increase primarily due to $99.1 million of net revenues from the acquired VI Business, higher sales volumes of existing products, and favorable foreign-currency fluctuations.

Decrease primarily due to 2025 tariffs, amortization of the VI Business purchase-accounting inventory and intangible step-up, higher quality-remediation and excess/obsolete inventory charges, and higher logistics/distribution costs.

SG&A rose on VI integration/amortization expenses and unfavorable FX (versus a prior-year hedge benefit); $16.8M of restructuring/separation costs and a $29.0M valuation-allowance adjustment on Strategic Divestitures assets held for sale added further pressure.

drivers.metric: Income from continuing operations before interest and taxes
drivers.explanation: Gross-margin compression (tariffs, VI step-up amortization) plus higher SG&A and R&D tied to VI integration outweighed the revenue gain from the acquisition.

Increase attributable to favorable working-capital changes — lower inventory cash outflows and higher accounts payable/accrued expenses from lower employee-benefit and compensation payments — partially offset by unfavorable operating results.
Decline driven mainly by $53.5 million in net payments on matured cross-currency swaps designated as net investment hedges and $18.8 million of capital expenditures.
Higher year-over-year mainly from borrowings used to fund the VI Business acquisition, per the filing's discussion of an increased average outstanding debt balance.

Year-over-year decline reflects cumulative FY2025 net losses — including the Q4 2025 valuation-allowance-driven loss — plus quarterly dividends since Q1 2025, exceeding any offsetting comprehensive income.
